sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: last30days is a skill for AI agents such as Claude Code and Codex that researches what people have said about any topic in the last 30 days. It searches Reddit, Hacker News, X, YouTube, Polymarket, GitHub and many other sources, and ranks findings by real engagement like upvotes and likes.
sixtySeconds.problem: Search engines favour editorial content and model training data lags behind current events. last30days pulls recent discussion from many platforms that no single search tool covers and has your agent write a cited brief.
whoFor: People preparing for meetings or sales calls
Researchers tracking fast-moving topics like AI
Anyone who wants a quick briefing on recent events
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for recent, people-ranked research inside the agent you already use. Reddit, Hacker News, Polymarket and GitHub work with no keys; other sources need keys or tools.
requirements: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI or another Agent Skills host
Optional API keys or tools for extra sources (X, YouTube via yt-dlp, ScrapeCreators, Brave and more)

overview: You type /last30days followed by a topic, such as a person, company or product. The skill searches many sources, scores results by engagement, and your agent writes a brief with the best quotes on their own lines, Polymarket odds where relevant and, for listed companies, the 30-day share price next to the S&P 500.

With zero configuration it uses Reddit, Hacker News, Polymarket, GitHub, StockTwits and, for companies, patent filings and careers pages. A first-run setup wizard installs free CLIs for arXiv, Techmeme and Yahoo Finance and helps you unlock X, YouTube, TikTok and others with your own keys.

It also has a discovery mode for questions like what is exploding in AI agents, JSON output for workflows, optional SQLite storage for tracking topics over time, and a local research library feed. Research files are saved to ~/Documents/Last30Days/ by default.
